What is anamorphic de-squeeze?

Anamorphic lenses squeeze the image horizontally to capture a wider field of view on a normal sensor. This look is popular with filmmakers using mobile anamorphic lenses from Moment, Sirui, Moondog Labs, and similar brands. Without de-squeezing, footage looks tall and skinny.

De-squeezing stretches the image back horizontally to the intended cinematic aspect ratio, such as 2.39:1, so the final frame looks natural, wide, and professional.

Recommended settings

1.33× Classic

Best for Moment-style mobile anamorphic lenses.

Use the 1.33× preset for quick correction and preview.

1.5× / 1.55×

Useful for some mobile and compact anamorphic adapters.

Choose the matching preset or use custom ratio.

1.8×

For stronger squeeze looks and wider cinematic framing.

Preview before export to confirm composition.

2.0×

Common for classic cinema anamorphic workflows.

Use 2.0× when footage appears heavily squeezed.

Custom

When your lens doesn’t match a standard preset.

Use custom ratio to dial in the exact stretch.

When to use Web Studio vs native apps

Web Studio

Best for quick browser previews, client links, small batches, and fast correction without installing anything.

iPhone / iPad

Best for mobile shooting, fast preview, live monitoring, and on-set workflows.

Android

Best for live desqueeze, quick correction, and mobile creator workflows.

Windows

Best for desktop batch processing, longer clips, and post-production workflows.

Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut — or DeSqueeze Studio?

You can manually de-squeeze footage inside an editor by adjusting horizontal scale or pixel aspect ratio. That works well for full finishing. But for fast previews, client checks, batch conversion, and corrected files before editing, DeSqueeze Studio is faster: choose ratio, preview, export.
